Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Velvety olive-green to dark brown circular spots on leaf surfaces that turn corky and cause premature defoliation.
organic_controls: Spray liquid copper soap or sulfur sprays before bloom.
Apply bio-fungicides containing Bacillus subtilis.
Prune lower branches to maximize canopy airflow.
chemical_controls: Apply myclobutanil, captan, or mancozeb according to local spray schedule guidelines.
prevention: Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn to eliminate overwintering ascospores.
Choose scab-resistant varieties like Liberty, Freedom, or Enterprise.

Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: Small purple spots enlarging into frogeye circular lesions with tan centers and dark margins; can spread to fruit rot.
organic_controls: Prune dead or diseased wood during the dormant season.
Spray copper-based fungicides at bud break.
chemical_controls: Fungicides containing thiophanate-methyl, captan, or strobilurins (pyraclostrobin).
prevention: Remove mummified apples and dead twigs from the tree canopy.
Disinfect pruning shears with 70% isopropyl alcohol between cuts.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Bright yellow-orange or rust-colored spots on upper leaf surfaces, developing raised tube-like fungal aecia on the underside.
organic_controls: Apply sulfur or copper fungicides when orange gelatinous galls appear on nearby junipers.
chemical_controls: Immunox (myclobutanil), chlorothalonil, or trifloxystrobin at early pink bud stage.
prevention: Remove eastern red cedar or juniper trees within a 1-mile radius where practical.
Plant rust-resistant cultivars (e.g., Gala, McIntosh are susceptible; Redfree and Liberty are resistant).

Apple___healthy.symptoms: Vibrant green, uniform texture, no discoloration or fungal lesions observed.
organic_controls: Maintain routine balanced nutrition (NPK with trace micronutrients).
chemical_controls: No chemical intervention required.
prevention: Continue regular monitoring, maintain balanced tree pruning, and ensure adequate drip irrigation.

Blueberry___healthy.symptoms: Lush green foliage, normal leaf expansion, no necrotic spotting or chlorosis.
organic_controls: Maintain acidic soil pH (4.5 - 5.5) with pine needle or peat mulch.
chemical_controls: No chemical intervention required.
prevention: Maintain consistent drip moisture; avoid waterlogging; inspect periodically for blueberry maggot or mummy berry.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White to light gray powdery fungal patches covering leaf surfaces, causing leaf curling and upward cupping.
organic_controls: Apply neem oil, horticultural oils, or potassium bicarbonate solutions.
Introduce sulfur dust prior to high humidity periods.
chemical_controls: Apply myclobutanil, tebuconazole, or quinoxyfen according to agricultural label.
prevention: Prune dense branches to allow sunlight penetration and wind drying.
Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation.

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.symptoms: Glossy, vibrant green foliage with healthy margins and firm venation.
organic_controls: Provide organic compost mulch around drip line.
chemical_controls: No chemical intervention required.
prevention: Maintain regular monitoring for black cherry aphid and prune dead limbs yearly.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.symptoms: Narrow, rectangular, tan-to-gray lesions restricted by leaf veins; can coalesce causing broad leaf blighting.
organic_controls: Incorporate crop residues deep into soil to speed microbial decomposition of overwintered spores.
chemical_controls: Apply triazole and strobilurin premix fungicides (e.g., azoxystrobin + propiconazole) at tasseling/VT stage.
prevention: Rotate with non-host crops (soybeans, alfalfa) for at least two consecutive seasons.
Select corn hybrids with high Gray Leaf Spot tolerance.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.symptoms: Cinnamon-brown to golden, powdery, raised pustules (uredinia) bursting on both upper and lower leaf surfaces.
organic_controls: Apply bio-control agents like Bacillus amyloliquefaciens in early vegetative growth.
chemical_controls: Foliar fungicides such as pyraclostrobin or fluxapyroxad when pustules appear before silking.
prevention: Plant resistant corn hybrids containing Rp resistance genes.
Plant early to avoid peak mid-summer airborne spore flights.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Large, cigar-shaped or elliptical grayish-green to tan lesions (1-6 inches long) that rapidly destroy photosynthetic leaf area.
organic_controls: Till debris under after harvest.
Apply copper or biological foliar sprays at early onset.
chemical_controls: Apply azoxystrobin, pyraclostrobin, or metconazole during vegetative and early reproductive stages.
prevention: Utilize multi-gene resistant seed varieties (Ht1, Ht2, Ht3).
Avoid continuous corn monoculture.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.symptoms: Vigorous dark green leaf blades, robust midrib structure, zero necrotic spotting.
organic_controls: Apply nitrogen side-dressing and organic seaweed extract for balanced growth.
chemical_controls: No chemical intervention required.
prevention: Ensure adequate soil drainage, balanced macro-nutrients, and scouting at silking stage.

Grape___Black_rot.symptoms: Small reddish-brown circular spots on leaves with black fruiting bodies (pycnidia) in a ring; shrivels berries into black mummies.
organic_controls: Apply copper sulfate or lime-sulfur sprays before bud-break.
Remove all dried berry mummies from vines during winter pruning.
chemical_controls: Mancozeb, myclobutanil, or azoxystrobin applied from 1-inch shoot growth through post-bloom.
prevention: Canopy management: shoot thinning and leaf pulling around fruit clusters to accelerate dew drying.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).symptoms: Tiger-stripe patterns on leaves (interveinal chlorosis and necrosis); dark brown or purple speckling on grapes.
organic_controls: Paint pruning wounds with wound sealants containing Trichoderma harzianum.
Avoid pruning during wet weather.
chemical_controls: No direct chemical cure for established systemic wood infections; preventative wound protection is vital.
prevention: Practice double-pruning; sanitize cutting tools between vines; rogue out chronically dying vines.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.symptoms: Large, irregular reddish-brown to dark necrotic spots with distinct dark margins, leading to early leaf yellowing and drop.
organic_controls: Bordeaux mixture or copper hydroxide sprays applied in late spring.
chemical_controls: Foliar applications of thiophanate-methyl, mancozeb, or strobilurin fungicides.
prevention: Improve air circulation through canopy trimming; clear fallen leaves from under trellises.

Grape___healthy.symptoms: Uniformly green palmate leaf surface, crisp margins, clear venation, intact leaf petiole.
organic_controls: Apply organic foliar compost tea and maintain balanced vine vigor.
chemical_controls: No chemical intervention required.
prevention: Maintain consistent trellis training, weed control below canopy, and monitor for early fungal pressure.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).pathogen_type: Bacteria (Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus, vectored by Asian citrus psyllid)
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).symptoms: Asymmetric blotchy mottling across leaf veins, yellowing veins, stunted leaves, small lopsided bitter fruit.
organic_controls: Release beneficial parasitoid wasps (Tamarixia radiata) against psyllids.
Apply foliar nutritional sprays (zinc, manganese, iron) to support tree resilience.
chemical_controls: Target vector control: systematic insecticides (imidacloprid, thiamethoxam, bifenthrin) targeting psyllids.
prevention: Use certified disease-free nursery stock.
Rogue and destroy verified infected trees to prevent grove-wide transmission.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, water-soaked angular dark purple or brown spots that drop out, creating a shot-hole appearance on leaves.
organic_controls: Apply chelated copper sprays at petal fall and shuck split.
chemical_controls: Oxytetracycline (Mycoshield) or copper bactericides during damp vegetative growth.
prevention: Plant in well-drained orchard soil; avoid excessive nitrogen fertilizer; choose resistant cultivars.

Peach___healthy.symptoms: Deep green, lanceolate leaf blades, smooth serrated borders, healthy petioles.
organic_controls: Apply organic mulch and balanced organic fertilizer.
chemical_controls: No chemical intervention required.
prevention: Conduct routine dormant oil sprays to manage scale and mites; ensure adequate summer watering.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, circular, water-soaked or translucent spots turning dark brown with yellow halos, leading to leaf drop.
organic_controls: Copper bactericide combined with Bacillus subtilis foliar spray.
chemical_controls: Fixed copper tank-mixed with mancozeb for synergistic bactericidal efficacy.
prevention: Use certified pathogen-free treated seed; sanitize stakes and drip lines; avoid working in fields when foliage is wet.

Pepper,_bell___healthy.symptoms: Uniform green elliptical leaves, strong turgor pressure, clean margins with no spotting.
organic_controls: Maintain consistent organic calcium and magnesium supplementation.
chemical_controls: No chemical intervention required.
prevention: Use drip irrigation; maintain plastic or straw mulch to prevent soil-splash pathogens.

Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Concentric brown to black target-board rings on older lower leaves, often surrounded by a chlorotic yellow halo.
organic_controls: Apply copper soap or bio-fungicide (Trichoderma) at first sign of lower leaf spotting.
Prune lower yellowing foliage.
chemical_controls: Chlorothalonil, azoxystrobin, or difenoconazole applied every 7-10 days under humid conditions.
prevention: Practice a 3-year crop rotation avoiding solanaceous crops; maintain optimal plant nitrogen to delay plant senescence.

Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Rapidly expanding water-soaked pale green or brown lesions with fuzzy white sporulation on the underside in humid conditions; destroys crops rapidly.
organic_controls: Apply copper sulfate or copper hydroxide immediately before predicted rainy periods.
chemical_controls: Mandipropamid, cymoxanil, dimethomorph, or metalaxyl/mefenoxam fungicides.
prevention: Plant only certified disease-free seed tubers; eliminate cull piles; destroy infected plants immediately upon confirmation.

Potato___healthy.symptoms: Compound leaves with rich green pinnate leaflets, strong vigor, no necrotic lesions.
organic_controls: Support tuber bulking with organic potassium and well-rotted compost.
chemical_controls: No chemical intervention required.
prevention: Hill potatoes adequately to protect tubers; monitor weather-based late blight forecast models.

Raspberry___healthy.symptoms: Healthy trifoliate leaves with serrated margins, light pubescent undersides, vigorous cane extension.
organic_controls: Add organic aged wood chips and bone meal around root zone.
chemical_controls: No chemical intervention required.
prevention: Trellis canes to maintain upright growth and open air flow; thin old canes after fruiting.

Soybean___healthy.symptoms: Trifoliate leaves with deep emerald color, smooth blade surfaces, no defoliation or pustules.
organic_controls: Inoculate seed with Bradyrhizobium japonicum for natural nitrogen fixation.
chemical_controls: No chemical intervention required.
prevention: Scout regularly for bean leaf beetle and frogeye leaf spot; maintain weed-free canopy rows.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: Talcum powder-like white fungal colonies on both surfaces of leaves and stems, turning leaves yellow and crispy.
organic_controls: Spray dilute milk-water solution (40:60 ratio) in sunlight.
Apply potassium bicarbonate, neem oil, or sulfur dust.
chemical_controls: Myclobutanil, triflumizole, or quinoxyfen.
prevention: Select PM-resistant squash cultivars; space plants widely to reduce humidity; water exclusively at soil level.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.symptoms: Numerous small, irregular purplish spots on upper leaf surfaces that enlarge and turn dark brown, giving the foliage a scorched look.
organic_controls: Apply copper-based fungicides after spring growth commences.
Prune and destroy scorched leaves during renovation.
chemical_controls: Captan, thiophanate-methyl, or pyraclostrobin sprays.
prevention: Plant in full sun in raised beds with good soil drainage; avoid overhead irrigation; renovate strawberry beds annually.

Strawberry___healthy.symptoms: Vibrant trifoliate leaves, bright green glossy leaflets with pronounced saw-toothed edges, sturdy runners.
organic_controls: Provide organic straw mulch to keep leaves and fruit elevated off bare soil.
chemical_controls: No chemical intervention required.
prevention: Ensure regular drip watering and inspect crowns periodically for spider mites or crown rot.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, angular, dark brown to black greasy water-soaked spots on leaves; spots may coalesce causing severe leaf blight.
organic_controls: Apply copper octanoate (copper soap) tank-mixed with biological Bacillus amyloliquefaciens.
chemical_controls: Fixed copper combined with mancozeb applied at 7-day intervals during wet periods.
prevention: Use hot-water treated or certified disease-free seeds; avoid overhead sprinkler watering; rotate away from nightshades.

Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown concentric ring lesions (bullseye pattern) developing on older bottom leaves first, with surrounding chlorosis.
organic_controls: Strip off bottom 12 inches of foliage as plant grows.
Apply copper soap or Serenade bio-fungicide weekly.
chemical_controls: Daconil (chlorothalonil), Quadris (azoxystrobin), or mancozeb.
prevention: Stake and prune plants for maximum airflow; apply heavy organic straw or plastic mulch to block soil splash; rotate crops.

Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Irregular water-soaked greasy gray-green lesions on leaves and stems that turn dark brown; white fungal fluff visible under leaves in high humidity.
organic_controls: Apply preventative copper hydroxide thoroughly before cool, wet weather sets in.
chemical_controls: Cymoxanil (Curzate), chlorothalonil, or Revus (mandipropamid) immediately upon disease alert.
prevention: Scout daily during wet, overcast weather; eliminate volunteer potato and tomato plants; destroy infected plants immediately.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale green or yellowish spots with indefinite margins on upper leaf surfaces; velvety olive-green to brown mold on the undersides.
organic_controls: Improve greenhouse ventilation and reduce relative humidity below 85%.
Apply copper or potassium bicarbonate foliar sprays.
chemical_controls: Fungicides containing chlorothalonil, mancozeb, or cyazofamid.
prevention: Increase plant spacing; use greenhouse circulating fans; select resistant cultivars with Cf resistance genes.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Numerous small circular spots (1/8 inch) with dark margins and gray/tan centers dotted with tiny black pycnidia specs.
organic_controls: Remove lower affected leaves promptly.
Spray copper fungicides starting when first cluster flowers emerge.
chemical_controls: Chlorothalonil, mancozeb, or tebuconazole.
prevention: Never overhead water; mulch soil base thoroughly; sanitize tomato cages and stakes yearly with bleach solution.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.symptoms: Fine yellow or white stippling (pinpoint flecks) on upper leaf surfaces; fine silk webbing on leaf undersides and branch crotches.
organic_controls: Release predatory mites (Phytoseiulus persimilis).
Apply insecticidal soap, rosemary oil, or neem oil sprays targeting leaf undersides.
chemical_controls: Acaricides such as abamectin, bifenazate, or spiromesifen.
prevention: Avoid hot, dry dust buildup around crop perimeter; do not over-apply synthetic pyrethroids which wipe out natural predators.

Tomato___Target_Spot.symptoms: Brown pinpoint lesions enlarging into circular lesions with light brown centers and dark concentric rings; often causes leaf perforation and defoliation.
organic_controls: Apply copper-based fungicides and improve canopy aeration.
chemical_controls: Azoxystrobin + difenoconazole, fluopyram, or chlorothalonil.
prevention: Maintain balanced plant nutrition; avoid excessive nitrogen; implement 3-year solanaceous crop rotation.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.pathogen_type: Virus (Begomovirus, vectored by Silverleaf Whitefly Bemisia tabaci)
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Severe plant stunting, erect bushy shoots, upward leaf curling, yellow leaf margins, flower drop and yield failure.
organic_controls: Use yellow sticky traps to capture whiteflies.
Spray insecticidal soaps or horticultural oils to suppress whitefly nymphs.
chemical_controls: Systemic neonicotinoids or pyriproxyfen to control whitefly populations.
prevention: Install fine insect-proof mesh netting in nursery beds; plant TYLCV-resistant tomato hybrids (e.g., Tygress, Skyway, Charger).

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Mottled light and dark green mosaic patterns on leaves, fern-like distortion (shoestring leaves), and internal browning of fruit.
organic_controls: No chemical or organic cure exists once a plant is systemically infected; rogue and destroy infected plants.
chemical_controls: Disinfect tools and hands in non-fat dry milk solution (20%) to neutralize viral transmission during pruning.
prevention: Prohibit tobacco smoking/vaping near plants; use certified virus-free seed; plant ToMV-resistant cultivars (Tm-2 gene).

Tomato___healthy.symptoms: Deep green serrated foliage, vigorous stem growth, absence of leaf spotting, curling, or chlorosis.
organic_controls: Apply balanced organic compost and maintain regular calcium levels to prevent blossom end rot.
chemical_controls: No chemical intervention required.
prevention: Maintain consistent drip irrigation, mulch soil, and prune sucker shoots for optimal canopy airflow.
